question: A train running at 75 km/hr crosses another train running at 30 km/hr in the same direction in 108 seconds. If the length of the fast-moving train is 950 m, then what is the length (in m) of the slow-moving train?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Relative speed = 75 − 30 = 45 km/hr = 45 × (5/18) = 12.5 m/s.

Total distance covered = Relative speed × Time = 12.5 × 108 = 1350 m.

Length of slow train = Total distance − Length of fast train.

Length of slow train = 1350 − 950 = 400 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 400 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of fast train (v₁) = 75 km/hr

Speed of slow train (v₂) = 30 km/hr

Length of fast train (L₁) = 950 m

Time to cross (T) = 108 seconds

**Formula Used:**

Relative speed (same direction) = v₁ − v₂

Total distance = L₁ + L₂ = Relative speed × Time

 
 Fast Train: 950 m
 
• 
 

 75 km/hr
 
 
 Slow Train: L m
 
• 
 

 30 km/hr

 Relative Speed = 75 − 30 = 45 km/hr

**Calculations:**

⇒ Relative speed = 75 − 30 = 45 km/hr

⇒ Convert km/hr to m/s: 45 × (5/18) = 12.5 m/s

⇒ Total Distance = 12.5 × 108 = 1350 m

⇒ Let the length of the slow train be L₂.

⇒ Total Distance = Length of fast train (L₁) + Length of slow train (L₂)

⇒ 1350 = 950 + L₂

⇒ L₂ = 1350 − 950 = 400 m

**∴ The correct answer is 400 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed in Opposite Directions

When two objects move in opposite directions, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds (v₁ + v₂).

Conversion of Speed Units

To convert km/hr to m/s, multiply the speed by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18/5.

Trains Crossing a Stationary Object

When a train crosses a stationary object with length (like a platform or bridge), the total distance covered is the length of the train plus the length of the object.
